edges.description: Degeneration of ninth-to-twelfth cranial nerve motor nuclei directly causes bulbar palsy.
Seventh (facial) cranial nerve motor nucleus involvement produces bilateral facial muscle weakness.
Hypoglossal (twelfth cranial nerve) motor neuron loss produces neurogenic atrophy of the tongue.
Hypoglossal motor neuron denervation causes spontaneous discharges manifesting as tongue fasciculations.
Lower cranial nerve weakness of speech musculature directly causes dysarthria.
Tenth cranial nerve / bulbar motor weakness reduces vocal loudness (hypophonia).
Corticospinal tract involvement manifests clinically as abnormal pyramidal signs on neurological examination.
Corticospinal tract upper motor neuron dysfunction disinhibits the extensor plantar reflex (Babinski sign).
Auditory neural dysfunction in the spiral ganglion / cochlear nerve pathway directly produces bilateral sensorineural hearing impairment.
Degeneration of retinal ganglion axons in MMNDV manifests clinically as bilateral optic atrophy.
Optic nerve degeneration in MMNDV causes mild visual acuity impairment in most affected variant patients.
Cerebellar dysfunction in the MMNDV subset manifests clinically as gait ataxia.

nodes.description: Universal auditory neural dysfunction across MMND is characterized physiologically by preserved distortion-product otoacoustic emissions (intact outer hair cell function) paired with impaired auditory brainstem responses, localizing the hearing defect to spiral ganglion / eighth-nerve auditory neurons rather than cochlear outer hair cells.

evidence.snippet: The results of the distortion product (DP) otoacoustic emissions (OAE) and auditory brain stem response (ABR) were available for the 20 ears. The most significant finding was the presence of robust OAEs in the presence of impaired AFA (ranging from mild to profound degree of SN hearing loss) in all. Thus, DPOAE and ABR demonstrated a neural dysfunction.

nodes.description: The primary cause of MMND remains unidentified. Sequencing of the riboflavin transporter genes SLC52A1, SLC52A2, and SLC52A3 (causative of phenotypically overlapping riboflavin transporter deficiency / Brown-Vialetto-Van Laere syndrome) and screening for C9ORF72 repeat expansions have been negative in familial and sporadic MMND cohorts, indicating a distinct genetic and/or environmental upstream insult targeting selective motor, auditory, and (in MMNDV) optic and cerebellar pathways.
